name: Nivolumab
route_note: IV infusion every 2 or 4 weeks; subcutaneous form with hyaluronidase (Opdivo Qvantig)
owner: Bristol Myers Squibb (Ono Pharmaceutical in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan)

discovery.by: Tasuku Honjo and colleagues (Kyoto University) discovered PD-1
discovery.note: Nivolumab is a fully human IgG4 anti-PD-1 antibody generated by Medarex in collaboration with Ono.

tagline: First PD-1 inhibitor approved, active across many cancer types
summary: Nivolumab is a fully human IgG4 monoclonal antibody that blocks the PD-1 checkpoint receptor on T cells. First approved in Japan in 2014 for melanoma, it is used across melanoma, lung, kidney, head and neck, oesophageal, gastric, bladder and liver cancers and Hodgkin lymphoma.
mechanism: PD-1 is an inhibitory receptor on activated T cells. Its ligands PD-L1 and PD-L2, often expressed by tumour and myeloid cells, suppress T-cell signalling and cause T-cell exhaustion within tumours.

Nivolumab binds PD-1 and blocks its interaction with both ligands, restoring the effector function of tumour-specific T cells. The IgG4 backbone (with a hinge-stabilising mutation) minimises Fc-mediated killing of the T cells it binds.
uses: Non-small cell lung cancer (metastatic, neoadjuvant, perioperative)
Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma

history.title: PD-1 discovered
history.detail: Honjo's group identifies PD-1 (programmed death-1) in apoptotic T-cell hybridomas.

history.title: Ono–Medarex collaboration
history.detail: Ono and Medarex agree to develop the anti-PD-1 antibody; BMS acquires Medarex in 2009.

history.title: Phase 1 results
history.detail: Topalian et al. report durable responses in melanoma, lung and kidney cancer.

history.title: First approval
history.detail: Approved in Japan in July for melanoma; the FDA grants accelerated approval in December.

history.title: Lung cancer
history.detail: Approved for previously treated squamous NSCLC after CheckMate 017 showed a survival benefit.

history.title: Nobel Prize
history.detail: Tasuku Honjo shares the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with James Allison.

history.title: Neoadjuvant NSCLC
history.detail: Approved with chemotherapy before surgery for resectable NSCLC (CheckMate 816).

history.title: Opdualag
history.detail: A fixed-dose combination with the anti-LAG-3 antibody relatlimab is approved for melanoma.

history.title: Subcutaneous form
history.detail: FDA approves Opdivo Qvantig, nivolumab with hyaluronidase for subcutaneous injection.

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

serious: Immune-mediated endocrinopathies (thyroiditis, hypophysitis, adrenal insufficiency, type 1 diabetes)

facts: Nivolumab (in Japan) was the first PD-1 inhibitor approved anywhere in the world.
Its 'Ono' and 'Medarex' origins split commercial rights between Ono in parts of Asia and BMS elsewhere.
